supporting_observations.claim: Tara Nguyen created temp.jsmith on the domain controller, and the new account was added to the Contractors group. This matches the stated temporary-account naming and group-membership practice.
From WS-TNGUYEN-01, Tara launched Group Policy Management (gpmc.msc) at high integrity and the process communicated with DC-LV-01 over RPC, SMB, and LDAP.

Tara initiated Remote Desktop sessions from WS-TNGUYEN-01 to DC-LV-01 and FILE-LV-01. The supplied practice says remote administration is performed only from WS-KORTEGA-01 by the IT administrator, so this activity is inconsistent with the stated practice.
A UserAssist registry record on WS-TNGUYEN-01 contains an encoded path that decodes to Windows PowerShell, but this record alone does not establish the command or its effect.

The evidence supports escalating as malicious because the help-desk user's high-integrity GPMC activity and RDP access to domain and file servers conflict with the supplied role and remote-administration practices, even though the account creation itself fits the stated process.

known_telemetry_limitations: The Sysmon PowerShell-related record is a UserAssist registry update, not a process-creation record with command line or outcome (S12-00068); the Windows security query returned no PowerShell matches.
The observed SSH record is a process-termination event and does not reveal its command line, destination, or purpose (S12-00055).
FILE-LV-01 Sysmon records in the window show Tara's interactive session setup but no subsequent user-launched command in the returned records (S12-00043, S12-00045, S12-00047).
The available records do not establish what changes, if any, were made through GPMC or during the RDP sessions (S12-00015, S12-00017, S12-00038, S12-00042).
claims_not_established: Whether Tara's credentials or workstation were compromised, or whether Tara performed these actions herself.
Whether the GPMC session changed a Group Policy Object or performed another administrative action.
What commands, if any, were run in PowerShell or Command Prompt, and whether those commands caused system changes.
Whether the RDP sessions accessed or modified sensitive files, services, or scheduled jobs.

Whether temp.jsmith was created for an approved contractor request; the account name and Contractors membership are consistent with policy but do not establish authorization for this specific account.
additional_evidence_needed: Validate the account request and change/ticket record for temp.jsmith, including the intended contractor, approval, and account expiration.
Collect DC-LV-01 Group Policy audit records and GPO change history around 13:53 UTC, including the identity and details of any changes.
Collect complete RDP session activity and relevant security, file-access, and application logs from DC-LV-01 and FILE-LV-01 for Tara's sessions.
Collect PowerShell Operational logs, process-creation telemetry, command history, and endpoint forensic data from WS-TNGUYEN-01 to determine what PowerShell or Command Prompt activity occurred.
Determine the SSH command, destination, and authentication details associated with Tara's session on WS-TNGUYEN-01.
